title: paged-kv: reallocator + pinning to reduce fragmentation, reuse hot blocks, and cut GPU-host transfers
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: the paged KV cache has shown increasing memory fragmentation and allocation overhead under bursty, high-concurrency workloads. That leads to extra memcpy/transfer work between CPU and GPU when blocks are evacuated, and observable p95 latency regressions on serving paths that rely on long KV chains. Motivation: reduce allocation churn and unnecessary evictions, make hot pages stay resident, and provide deterministic reuse to reduce worst-case tail latency.

Summary of changes: implemented a new block reallocator and pin manager for the paged KV cache. Key pieces: BlockAllocator (size-classed free lists + contiguous free spans), BlockPool (per-device pool for reuse to avoid cross-device allocations), PinManager (reference-counted pinning of blocks used by in-flight requests), and an atomic reservation API to avoid races during concurrent alloc/free. Integration touches the existing kv/paged_cache.cc to wire allocation/reuse paths and the scheduler heuristics so the runtime prefers pinned blocks for hot KV prefixes. A feature flag (pinned_kv_v2) gates the rollout.

Design notes: - Size classes tuned for observed page sizes (128B/512B/2KB/8KB) to reduce internal fragmentation. - Reallocator attempts to coalesce adjacent free blocks to satisfy larger requests and keep fragmentation low. - Pinning is lightweight: a block can have a short-lived pin (auto-unpin on request completion) or a long-lived lease (for cache warmups). Pins prevent eviction and skip expensive GPU->host transfers. - Eviction now uses a two-pass policy: prefer unpinned cold blocks, and when forced, write-back/push hot pinned blocks to a spill region instead of synchronous host copies. - Atomic reservation ensures that two concurrent request threads don't both allocate and then race to copy into the same block; a reservation token is returned and either converted to a block or released.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for BlockAllocator coalescing and reservation semantics, integration tests exercising pin/unpin with concurrent alloc/free, and added a stress job in perf-canary that simulates high-QPS KV churn. One flaky test (kv_allocator_concurrency) surfaced on first CI run; root cause was a missing memory barrier in the reservation path and was fixed in subsequent commit. CI summary below.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on a 4-GPU Dedicated node under our "ask-heavy" synthetic trace show: - p95 latency: -9% (from 138ms to 126ms) - throughput: +12% sustained under 2k concurrent requests - memory fragmentation (estimated wasted bytes): -18% - block reuse rate (requests satisfied from free pool without fresh allocation): +34% Real-world canary in us-west-2 (20% of traffic, green path) confirms ~6% p95 improvement on customer traffic with no error increase. Details in the perf artifact link (see checks).

Rollout plan: enable pinned_kv_v2 behind config flag. Phases: (1) internal canary on dev cluster (done), (2) Dedicated canary 5% traffic for 48h, (3) ramp to 50% for a week, (4) full rollout. Fallback: flip pinned_kv_v2 off to revert quickly. Metrics to watch: kv_page_hits, kv_pin_evictions, kv_reservation_conflicts, mem_fragmentation_estimate, and end-to-end p95.

Backward compatibility: no API changes. Runtime option only.

Notes/links: Linear: ENG-3152 (reallocator design), ENG-3221 (pinning instrumentation). Support ticket SUP-4123 reported observed tail latency in production and motivated canary. Perf artifacts: ci/perf/artifacts/paged-kv-reallocator-2026-03-02.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and benchmark plan - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary run - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Docs updated (architecture KV page)

Small migration note: the existing on-disk spill format is unchanged but spill ordering differs slightly because pinned blocks are moved to the front of the spill queue to preserve hotness.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice end-to-end work. Two asks: (1) add a metric for reservation_conflicts and (2) ensure the reservation path is non-blocking in hot loops.
Asha Patel: Added kv_reservation_conflicts and made reservation switch to try-reserve w/ fast-fail; updated tests.
Liang Zhou: Found a subtle race where unpin during eviction could double-free a block; suggested using RC and a tombstone flag.
Asha Patel: Fixed with reference-counted pin + tombstone; added a stress test that reproduces the original failure before the fix.
Priya Menon: CI showed kv_allocator_concurrency flaky on the first run. After force-rerun, all checks passed. Please include note in PR about flaky test and fix.
Asha Patel: Root cause was missing acquire-release pair in reservation; added atomic fence and test; documented fix in the changelog.
benchmarks_summary: block reuse rate: +34% (requests satisfied without new allocation)
release_notes: Improved paged KV block allocator and pinning. Reduces memory fragmentation, cuts tail latency, and increases throughput under high-concurrency workloads. Opt-in via runtime flag pinned_kv_v2. Monitor kv_page_hits, kv_pin_evictions, kv_reservation_conflicts.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag pinned_kv_v2 can be toggled from Console or config. Watch kv_pin_evictions and mem_fragmentation_estimate during ramp. If any regression, flip the feature off to revert immediately.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: internal-only change with feature flag. Potential risk under extreme allocation pressure if coalescing heuristics mis-tuned; mitigated by canary and quick rollback.

authors_notes: Will follow up with a targeted postmortem if any unexpected regressions show up during Dedicated rollout. Perf artifacts and graphs are attached in CI.
